simple.meaning: אָנָה (ʼânâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to approach ; hence, to meet in various senses.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Exodus, 2 Kings, Psalms, Proverbs, beginning at Exodus 21:13. Its contexts include righteousness, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָנָה (H579).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָנָה (ʼânâh) / H579 is traced through Exodus 21:13, 2 Kings 5:7, Psalms 91:10, Proverbs 12:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to approach ; hence, to meet in various senses
definitions.usage: befall, deliver, happen, seek a quarrel.
definitions.full: H579. anah III. [ אָנָה ] verb be opportune, meet, encounter opportunely (Arabic the right time is come , or it is come to the right time , or to maturity , or is opportune ). Pi`el Perfect אִנָּה Exod 21:13 cause ( or allow ) to meet in א ׳הָאֱלֹהִים בְיָדוֺ (object omitted), i.e. without any purpose of the man to whom suffix Ref. Pu`al be allowed to meet, be sent, Imperfect יְאֻנֶּה Prov 12:21 (with ל ); 3 feminine singular תְּאֻנֶּה Psa 91:10 (with אֶל ), subject evil . Hithpa`el cause oneself to meet, seek occasion (= seek a quarrel with) followed by ל 2Kin 5:7 .
